equation_request.abstract: We describe a new method for the decomposition of an arbitrary $n$ qubit operator with entries in $\mathbb{Z}[i,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]$, i.e., of the form $\frac{a+b\sqrt{2}+i(c+d\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{2}^{k}}$, into Clifford+$T$ operators where $n\leq 2$. This method achieves a bound of $O(k)$ gates using at most one ancilla using decomposition into $1$- and $2$-level matrices which was first proposed by Giles and Selinger in [2].

specification.problem: Decompose an arbitrary n-qubit unitary (n<=2) with entries in Z[i,1/sqrt2], of the form (a+b sqrt2+i(c+d sqrt2))/sqrt2^k, exactly into a Clifford+T circuit with O(k) gates using at most one ancilla, via decomposition into 1- and 2-level matrices (Giles-Selinger approach).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement and gate-count claim only; the detailed decomposition algorithm is not in the abstract and is not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: integer coefficients of a matrix entry
denominator exponent (sqrt2 power) of the operator

equations.label: Entry form
equations.description: Form of each matrix entry in Z[i,1/sqrt2].

equations.label: Gate bound
equations.description: Claimed Clifford+T gate count with at most one ancilla.

registers.name: data
registers.role: qubits on which the target operator acts

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: optional helper qubit for Clifford+T synthesis of 2-level matrices

specification.initial_state: Data register in an arbitrary input state; ancilla (if used) in |0>.

steps.description: Take the unitary U with entries of the stated form (eq_1) and reduce it to a product of 1- and 2-level matrices over Z[i,1/sqrt2], following Giles-Selinger (details not given in abstract).
Implement each 1- and 2-level factor as a Clifford+T gate sequence, using at most one ancilla, so total gate count is O(k).

specification.measurement: None specified: this is a unitary synthesis task. For verification one could measure all data qubits (and the ancilla) in the computational basis after applying the circuit; the ancilla should return to |0> if used as a clean ancilla. This is an assumption, not from the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical work is the compilation: computing the 1-/2-level decomposition and gate sequences from the matrix entries (a,b,c,d,k). No measurement-outcome postprocessing is described.
assumptions: The operator is assumed unitary, as is needed for a circuit.
Plan is a high-level outline following the cited Giles-Selinger approach.
Measurement is only an optional verification choice; the abstract specifies none.
Ancilla is assumed to be returned to |0>.
